questions.prompt: Ice water sits in a glass on a hot day, and drops of water appear on the outside. Where do they come from?
choices: Water vapour in the air, cooled by the glass
The water leaks through the glass
questions.explain: Warm air touches the cold glass and the water vapour in it condenses into drops.

questions.prompt: You keep a plant in a dark cupboard for two weeks. What will most likely happen?
questions.explain: Without light a plant cannot make food or chlorophyll.

questions.prompt: You give a ball the same push on a carpet and on smooth ice. Where does it roll farther?
questions.explain: Ice has much less friction.

questions.prompt: You shake a can of fizzy drink and open it straight away. What happens?
questions.explain: Shaking releases dissolved gas as bubbles that push the liquid out.

questions.prompt: A bar magnet is cut in half. What do you get?
choices: Two smaller magnets, each with two poles
One north half and one south half
Two pieces that are not magnetic
questions.explain: Every piece of a magnet has a north and a south pole.

questions.prompt: Salt is spread on an icy road. What does it do?
choices: It lowers the freezing point so the ice melts
It makes the road warmer by burning
questions.explain: Salty water freezes at a lower temperature than pure water.

questions.prompt: You mix baking soda and vinegar in a bottle and seal it tightly. What is likely to happen?
choices: Nothing, the bottle stays the same
Pressure builds up and the cap may pop off
questions.explain: The reaction makes carbon dioxide gas, which needs space.

questions.prompt: You drop a hammer and a feather together on the Moon, where there is no air. Which lands first?
choices: They land at the same time
questions.explain: Without air resistance all objects fall at the same rate.

questions.prompt: You put a metal spoon and a wooden spoon in hot water. Which handle gets hot faster?
questions.explain: Metals are good conductors of heat.

questions.prompt: You rub a balloon on your hair and hold it near tiny paper bits. What happens?
choices: The paper jumps to the balloon
questions.explain: Rubbing builds up static electricity, which attracts light objects.

questions.prompt: An ice cube floats in a glass filled to the brim. When it melts, what happens to the water level?
questions.explain: Floating ice displaces its own weight in water, so melting changes nothing.

questions.prompt: On a sunny day, which T-shirt gets warmer in the Sun?
questions.explain: Dark colours absorb more light and turn it into heat.

questions.prompt: A car brakes suddenly and the passengers lurch forward. Why?
questions.explain: Objects keep moving unless a force stops them.

questions.prompt: A steel ball sinks but a huge steel ship floats. Why?
choices: The ship is shaped to hold lots of air, so it is less dense overall
Steel gets lighter in big pieces
The sea pushes harder on ships
questions.explain: Overall density matters, not just the material.

questions.prompt: You pour cooking oil onto water. What happens?
choices: The oil floats on top without mixing
The oil sinks to the bottom
questions.explain: Oil is less dense than water and does not mix with it.

questions.prompt: A rocket in empty space has nothing to push against. Can it still speed up?
choices: Only if it is near a planet
Yes, by pushing exhaust gas backwards
questions.explain: Newton’s third law: pushing gas back pushes the rocket forward.

questions.prompt: Water boils inside a pressure cooker. Compared with an open pot, the boiling point is…
questions.explain: More pressure means water needs more heat to boil.

questions.prompt: An ambulance siren passes you. What happens to its pitch?
questions.explain: The Doppler effect: sound waves bunch up when it approaches and spread out as it leaves.

questions.prompt: Two identical ice cubes sit at room temperature, one on a metal tray and one on a plastic plate. Which melts first?
questions.explain: Metal conducts heat from the room to the ice faster.

questions.prompt: You spin on a chair with your arms out, then pull your arms in. What happens to your spin?
questions.explain: Angular momentum is conserved: a smaller radius means a faster spin.

questions.prompt: A satellite orbits Earth. Why does it not fall to the ground?
choices: Its engines push it up all the time
It is falling, but moves sideways so fast that it keeps missing Earth
There is no gravity in space
questions.explain: An orbit is a continuous fall around the planet.

questions.prompt: Two bulbs are wired in parallel. You remove one. What happens to the other?
questions.explain: Each bulb has its own path for the current.

questions.prompt: Two bulbs are wired in series. You remove one. What happens to the other?
questions.explain: Removing one breaks the only path for the current.

questions.prompt: Equal amounts of a strong acid and a strong base are mixed. The pH ends up close to…
questions.explain: Neutralisation makes mostly water and salt.

questions.prompt: A sealed rigid container of gas is heated. What happens to the pressure inside?
questions.explain: Hotter molecules move faster and hit the walls harder.

questions.prompt: One bacterium divides into two every hour. About how many are there after 6 hours?
questions.explain: Doubling six times: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64.

questions.prompt: If Earth had no atmosphere, what colour would the daytime sky be?
questions.explain: The sky is blue because the atmosphere scatters blue light.

questions.prompt: A metal ring is cooled. What happens to the hole in the middle?
questions.explain: The whole ring contracts, including the hole.

questions.prompt: A 60 kg person visits the Moon, where gravity is about one sixth of Earth’s. What happens?
choices: Their mass stays 60 kg but their weight drops to about a sixth
questions.explain: Mass is the amount of matter; weight depends on gravity.

questions.prompt: The Sun suddenly vanished. About how long before Earth noticed the light going out?
questions.explain: Light takes about 8 minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth.

questions.prompt: The distance between two masses is doubled. What happens to the gravitational pull between them?
questions.explain: Gravity follows an inverse-square law.

questions.prompt: The volume of a gas at constant temperature is halved. What happens to its pressure?
questions.explain: Boyle’s law: pressure and volume are inversely related.

questions.prompt: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 10 years. How much is left after 20 years?
questions.explain: Each half-life halves what remains: 1/2 then 1/4.

questions.prompt: A mutation happens in a skin cell of a parent. Can it be passed to their children?
choices: Only if the child is a girl
No, only changes in egg or sperm cells are inherited
questions.explain: Only changes in reproductive cells (gametes) are passed on.

questions.prompt: Ignoring air, you drop a ball into a tunnel that goes straight through the centre of Earth. What does it do?
choices: It swings back and forth between the two ends
questions.explain: Gravity pulls it back toward the centre from either side.

questions.prompt: Two objects of different masses fall in a vacuum. Which has the greater acceleration?
questions.explain: Gravity gives every object the same acceleration, about 9.8 m/s².
